info.title: Task-Tracker API
info.description:
# Task-Tracker API

> **DE** · **EN** · **العربية** — a trilingual introduction follows.

---

## 🇩🇪 Deutsch

Die **Task-Tracker-API** ist die HTTP-Schnittstelle der mandantenfähigen
Aufgabenverwaltung. Dokumentiert sind die tatsächlichen HTTP-Endpunkte
(Next.js *Route Handler*): **OAuth/SSO-Anmeldung**, **Cron-/Sync-Webhooks**,
**Web-Push-Abonnements**, **Datei-Download**, **Mandantenwechsel** und **Logout**.

Die meisten schreibenden Operationen der Anwendung laufen über **Next.js Server
Actions** und sind bewusst *nicht* Teil dieser REST-Dokumentation — sie besitzen
keinen stabilen, extern aufrufbaren HTTP-Vertrag. Die zugehörigen
Validierungsschemata sind unter `components.schemas` als Datenmodelle abgebildet.

**Authentifizierung.** Benutzer-Sitzungen laufen über ein **httpOnly-Session-Cookie**
(`tt_session`, 30 Tage, serverseitig in der Datenbank hinterlegt). Cron-Endpunkte
sind über den Header `x-sync-secret` (gemeinsames Geheimnis) abgesichert. **JWT**
kommt ausschließlich im OAuth-`id_token` der Identity-Provider vor und wird
serverseitig verifiziert — die API akzeptiert **kein** clientseitig übergebenes
Bearer-JWT.

## 🇬🇧 English

The **Task-Tracker API** is the HTTP surface of the multi-tenant task-management
app. What is documented here are the real HTTP endpoints (Next.js *Route
Handlers*): **OAuth/SSO sign-in**, **cron/sync webhooks**, **Web-Push
subscriptions**, **file download**, **tenant switching** and **logout**.

Most write operations run through **Next.js Server Actions** and are deliberately
*out of scope* for this REST reference — they have no stable, client-callable HTTP
contract. The validation schemas those actions use are mirrored under
`components.schemas` as the domain models.

**Authentication.** User sessions use an **httpOnly session cookie** (`tt_session`,
30 days, backed by a database row). Cron endpoints are guarded by a shared-secret
header (`x-sync-secret`). **JWT** appears *only* inside the OAuth `id_token`
returned by identity providers and is verified server-side — the API does **not**
accept a client-supplied bearer JWT.

## 🇸🇦 العربية

**واجهة برمجة تطبيقات متعقّب المهام** هي الواجهة عبر HTTP لتطبيق إدارة المهام
متعدّد المستأجرين. المُوثَّق هنا هو النقاط الطرفية الفعلية عبر HTTP (معالِجات
المسارات في Next.js): **تسجيل الدخول عبر OAuth/SSO**، و**خطافات المزامنة
والمهام المجدولة (cron)**، و**اشتراكات الإشعارات الفورية (Web-Push)**، و**تنزيل
الملفات**، و**تبديل المستأجر**، و**تسجيل الخروج**.

تعمل معظم عمليات الكتابة في التطبيق عبر **إجراءات الخادم (Server Actions)** في
Next.js، وهي خارج نطاق هذا المرجع عن قصد لأنها لا تملك عقد HTTP مستقرًّا قابلًا
للاستدعاء من العميل. ومع ذلك، فإن مخطّطات التحقّق المستخدَمة في تلك الإجراءات
مُدرَجة ضمن `components.schemas` كنماذج بيانات.

**المصادقة.** تعتمد جلسات المستخدم على **كوكي جلسة من نوع httpOnly** (`tt_session`،
مدّته 30 يومًا، مدعوم بسجلّ في قاعدة البيانات). أمّا نقاط cron فمحميّة بترويسة
سرّ مشترك (`x-sync-secret`). يظهر **JWT** حصريًّا داخل `id_token` الخاص بـ OAuth
القادم من مزوّدي الهوية ويُتحقَّق منه في الخادم — والواجهة **لا** تقبل رمز JWT
من نوع bearer مُرسَلًا من العميل.

---

## Rate limits

The application layer does **not** currently enforce request rate limiting; there
is no per-IP or per-token quota, and endpoints do not emit `RateLimit-*` headers
or `429` responses. In production the service runs behind a **Caddy reverse
proxy** (see `next.config`), which is the recommended place to apply coarse
network-level limits. Practical bounds that *do* exist today:

| Guard | Where | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server-action body size | `next.config` `serverActions.bodySizeLimit` | **6 MB** per request |
| Attachment upload size | `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | **10 MB** per file |
| OAuth `state` lifetime | `tt_sso_state` cookie `maxAge` | **10 minutes** |
| Session lifetime | `tt_session` cookie / DB row | **30 days** |

If you add rate limiting, document the resulting `429` + `Retry-After` behaviour
here.

tags.description: Agent integration (Claude Code) via per-user machine tokens.

get.description: Kicks off the OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow: generates a CSRF `state`, stores it in the `tt_sso_state` cookie (10-min TTL) and redirects the browser to the provider's authorize URL. If the provider is unknown or unconfigured, redirects to `/login?sso=unavailable` instead.

302.description: Redirect to the provider's authorization endpoint.

Set-Cookie.description: Session / state cookie side-effects where applicable.

get.description: Provider redirect target for `response_type=code` (Azure-AD, Google, GitHub). Validates `state` against the `tt_sso_state` cookie, exchanges the code, resolves the user (link existing identity, route by email domain to a tenant, or auto-provision when enabled), then sets the `tt_session` cookie and redirects to `/`. On any failure redirects to `/login?sso={reason}`.

302.description: Success → redirect to `/` with a fresh `tt_session` cookie. Failure → redirect to `/login?sso={reason}` where reason ∈ {unavailable, state, exchange, profile, no_tenant, disabled, no_account}.

post.description: Provider redirect target for `response_mode=form_post` (Apple). Same logic as the GET callback but reads `code`/`state` from the posted form body.

Set-Cookie.description: Session / state cookie side-effects where applicable.

get.summary: MCP discovery — identity and available operations
get.description: Returns the user/tenant the token acts as, its scopes, and the operations it may call. Used by the MCP server (`mcp/task-tracker-mcp.mjs`) and as a connectivity check. See [MCP.md](https://github.com/tareq-fatal/task-tracker/blob/main/docs/MCP.md).

401.description: Missing, unknown, revoked or expired token — or its user is deactivated. All four are reported identically so the endpoint cannot be used to probe tokens.

post.description:
Single RPC entry point: `{ "op": "<name>", "params": { … } }`. Deliberately not a REST tree — an agent calls tools by name, so one dispatch point keeps the whole machine-facing surface to exactly one auth check and one scope check.

Read ops: `whoami`, `list_tasks`, `get_task`, `list_steps`, `list_projects`. Write ops (need the `write` scope): `create_task`, `update_task`, `add_comment`, `log_prompt`, `add_step`, `complete_step`, `upload_attachment`, `create_project`.

Every op inherits the token user's permissions: a task in another tenant reports `404 task not found`, never `403`.

params.description: Operation parameters; schema per op (strict — unknown keys are rejected).

400.description: Malformed body, missing `op`, or params that fail the op's schema.

example.error: invalid params: title — String must contain at least 1 character(s)

403.description: Token lacks the op's scope, or the user may not perform it.

404.description: Unknown op — or a task that does not exist *for this token's tenant*.

409.description: Blocked by the admin workflow gate (`TARGET_LOCKED`, `TODOS_OPEN`, `TIME_REQUIRED`).

413.description: Attachment exceeds the 10 MB upload limit.

415.description: Attachment MIME type is not on the allowlist.

post.description: Upserts the caller's browser push subscription (keyed by `endpoint`) so the server can deliver notifications. Requires an authenticated session.

delete.description: Deletes the caller's subscription for the given `endpoint`. Idempotent.

get.description: Streams an attachment as a forced download (`Content-Disposition: attachment`, `application/octet-stream`). Access is tenant-scoped: the caller must be in the attachment's tenant AND be an admin, the task creator, or the assignee.

403.description: Authenticated but not allowed to view the task.

404.description: Not found, wrong tenant, or file missing on disk.

get.description: Path-based tenant entry. For a BackendAdmin/SuperAdmin, sets the `tt_tenant` cookie to the given tenant slug and redirects to `/`. For other roles the cookie is left unchanged (they are hard-locked to their own tenant). Unauthenticated → `/login`.

302.description: Redirect to `/` (tenant cookie set for BackendAdmin) or `/login`.

Set-Cookie.description: Session / state cookie side-effects where applicable.

get.description: Destroys the current session (deletes the DB row and clears `tt_session`) and redirects to `/login`. A plain GET navigation so it works inside the Capacitor WebView, where form-POST Server Actions were unreliable.

Set-Cookie.description: Session / state cookie side-effects where applicable.

get.description: Returns this specification as JSON. Powers the Swagger-UI at `/api-docs`.

sessionCookie.name: tt_session
sessionCookie.description: Primary end-user authentication. An opaque, server-generated session token stored as an httpOnly cookie and backed by a `Session` row (30-day expiry). Set by password login (Server Action) or the OAuth callback; cleared by `GET /logout`. Not a JWT — the token carries no claims.

syncSecret.name: x-sync-secret
syncSecret.description: Shared-secret guard for machine-to-machine cron/sync endpoints. The value must equal the server's `SYNC_SECRET` env var. When `SYNC_SECRET` is unset the endpoints return `503`.

mcpToken.description: Per-user machine token for the MCP endpoint (`tt_mcp_…`), sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. Minted with `npm run mcp:token -- mint --user <username>`; only its SHA-256 hash is stored, so the value is shown exactly once. The token binds ONE user and ONE tenant — every call runs with that user's role inside that mandant and cannot widen either. Carries a `read` or `read,write` scope, and is refused once revoked, expired, or when its user is deactivated.

oauth2.description: SSO sign-in via an identity provider (Microsoft/Azure-AD, Google, GitHub, Apple). The browser is redirected through the provider; on return the server verifies the provider's `id_token` (a JWT) and issues its own `tt_session` cookie. This is a redirect flow driven by `/api/auth/{provider}/start` and `/api/auth/{provider}/callback`, not a token the client sends to this API.

TaskType.description: Issue hierarchy type (Epic > Story > Task > Subtask; Bug with Task).

Task.description: Task create/update payload (`taskSchema`). Duration fields accept shorthands ("4h", "1d", "90m") that are parsed to hours server-side.

description.example: Generate the 3.1 spec and serve Swagger-UI.

tags.description: Free tags, lowercase and without spaces. A comma-separated string is accepted too.

User.description: User create/update payload (`userSchema`). `email` and `password` may be empty strings: empty email = no email, empty password = a temporary one is generated.

Settings.description: Account settings (`settingsSchema`). `newPassword`, when present, must be ≥ 6 chars.

PushSubscription.description: W3C Push API subscription forwarded from the browser. Shape matches `PushSubscription.toJSON()`; the route reads `endpoint` and `keys.{p256dh,auth}`.

PushUnsubscribe.description: Endpoint identifying the subscription to remove.

CronResult.description: Result envelope from a cron/sync run. Extra keys depend on the job.

dueSoon.description: notifications job — reminders sent for soon-due tasks.

overdue.description: notifications job — reminders sent for overdue tasks.

ran.description: planner sync job — number of tenant syncs executed.

Error.description: Uniform error envelope returned by the JSON endpoints.
